raw_response:
I've been working this land for thirty years. I know these fields. My main business is the wheat-maize rotation — that's where the reliable money and food comes from. The 5.5 mu on the flat, good-soil plots go into that rotation every year without question. I've been using improved wheat seed (something like Jimai series — the seed station sells it, yields are better, I've seen it work on my neighbor's fields too). For maize I always go hybrid, Zhengdan 958 or similar — everyone around here uses it.

The 2 mu of cotton is hard work. Picking in August heat is brutal, and my second son works at the factory in town now, so I have less help. But I've grown cotton since I was young, I know how to do it, and when prices are decent it beats grain. I'll keep it but not expand it. I plough the cotton plots in spring — that field needs it, the soil compacts.

The remaining 1 mu in the low corner plot I put in mungbean. The soil there isn't worth the inputs for grain. We eat some, sell the rest at the market in town. I use old seed saved from last year, I don't buy new.

For fertilizer — I apply base compound fertilizer before sowing and topdress with urea. I've always done around 18-20 jin of pure nitrogen per mu for wheat and maize. Maybe the technicians say it's too much but my yields hold up. I can't afford to underfeed and get a poor harvest with seven mouths at home.

Irrigation from the well — wheat gets water three times (pre-sowing, jointing, heading), maize gets two (tasseling, grain fill). Water is getting harder to pump, the level is dropping year by year. I don't waste it.
